input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer, failing the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and incapable of falling within the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees), because it is a payment-delay charge rather than a termination fee. At fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a ten-day delay it is triggered by a minor breach and would exceed the remaining contract value within roughly seven weeks — walk-away territory. No other Customer-payable liquidated amount appears (Sections 9.4 and 10 contain no minimum or early-termination sums), and the SLA credits running to us are beneficial and not flagged. The redline makes the minimal operative change: it flips the payment obligation into a prohibition on any liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer, leaving Vendor's other late-payment remedies and the Section 7.3 interest reference untouched.
